name: Wilderlings
body:
Centuries ago, settlers seeking to make a home for themselves settled down in a lush forest. Unknown to them at the time, the forest was home to a wide variety of fey who lived in harmony with nature. While initial meetings were not without friction, in the generations since the settlers who remained came to embrace the fey ways and to be embraced by them in return. Now, their desc enda nts share an innate bond with the forest on a level normally only understood by druids and animals. They flit between dense trees as easily as a deer, and their fey heritage manifests itself as features that appear delicate to the point of being frail. This appearance is deceiving, however, as they share their ancestor’s supernatural resilience.

Wilderling settlements can be found in most large forests with a fey presence. They are often hard to spot from a distance, or at least hard to recognize as a series of dwellings—nest-like treehouses, burrows, and even dams are constructed in elegant imitations of animal shelters, though their interiors are deceptively cozy for their inescapable rusticness. These communities are often wary of outsiders, though the presence of animal companions or individuals with a strong connection to the natural world within a group goes a long way towards turning their caution into friendly curiosity. Those who help these communities and earn their respect may even find themselves being honored with a ceremony that imbues them with some small measure of the wilderling’s primal connection to the forest—a connection which sometimes blossoms into much more.

Wilderlings who do find themselves living a life beyond the woods almost always try to avoid being alone, the pack/tribe mentality being too instinctual to make a solitary life comfortable. Of those, the ones who don’t find the life of an adventurer appealing are highly prized as animal handlers and gardeners.

Physical Description: Every wilderling has a personal connection to the natural forces that shape the environment they have so well adapted to. Whether it is plant or animal, this connection manifests itself strongly in their appearance and varies widely from one individual to another. Some wilderlings can almost pass for half-elves, while others, especially older wilderlings, look so strange and exotic that they have a hard time fitting in outside wilderling communities.

Relations: Wilderlings get along well with most who aren’t despoiling nature. They have enjoyed good relations with elves & gnomes in the past, and they have a better track record with human towns and villages than with human cities. Most wilderlings will be a bit mistrustful of anyone they meet who looks too ‘civilized’.

Alignment & Religion: Wilderlings share a racial connection with nature, and you’d be hard pressed to find a single wilderling who doesn’t look to nature the way a priest looks to their god.

Adventurers: Wilderling adventurers are not unheard of, though few wilderlings are comfortable enough outside the canopy of the forest to pursue that path very far. Despite this, most of the outside world’s perception of wilderlings is shaped by the few such adventurers they produce, as few people have the cause or means to seek out their reclusive communities.

Male Names: Aelloch, Ersugal, Hymdar, Lachlan, Orlatz, Rakdus, Tamlyn

Female Names: Braithe, Dyrdri, Mellara, Prylwyn, Tendrys, Winowa

Traits

Wilderlings are defined by their class levels—they do not possess racial Hit Dice. All wilderlings have the following racial traits:

Ability Score Modifiers (0 RP): While undeniably graceful and charming, wilderlings are prone to thin, delicate builds. They gain +2 Dexterity, +2 Charisma but suffer -4 to Constitution
Fey (2 RP): Wilderlings are fey with the wilderling subtype.
Medium (0 RP): Wilderlings are Medium creatures and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.
Base Speed (0 RP): Wilderlings have a base speed of 30 feet.
Fey Damage Resistance (3 RP): Wilderlings gain DR 5/cold iron.
Forest Stride (Ex) (1 RP): Wilderlings can move through natural difficult terrain at their normal speed while within forests. Magically altered terrain affects them normally.
Bond of the Woods (Ex) (3 RP): At 1st level, a wilderling gains a choice between either Bond of Flora or Bond of Fauna as a bonus feat.

Call of the Wild, Book 1 – The Druid. © 2017 d20pfsrd.com Publishing; Author: Kalen Tessmann
